supported-platforms.statement: The platforms that can be connected to 3rd-Party App Governance are Atlassian, Databricks, GitHub, Google Workspace, Microsoft Azure, Okta, Salesforce and Slack.

quotes: You can connect the following platforms to 3rd-Party App Governance:
- Atlassian
- Databricks
- GitHub
- Google Workspace
- Microsoft Azure
- Salesforce
You can connect your Okta organization to Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance
You can connect your Slack organization to Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance

connecting-user.statement: Connecting to a platform needs a user with admin privileges on it, not necessarily the user used to sign in to 3rd-Party App Governance (some clients use dedicated service accounts). Onboarding can be self-onboarding or a concierge onboarding scheduled with Zscaler Support.

quotes: A user with admin privileges is required to connect to your platforms. This can be done with any user, not necessarily the user you used to sign in to 3rd-Party App Governance (some clients use dedicated service accounts).
You can choose between self-onboarding or scheduling a concierge onboarding with Zscaler Support.

platform-admin-roles.statement: The platform-side privileges each integration page requires are Atlassian Admin (with Jira User Access Admin, Confluence Product Admin and User Access Admin, and Jira Administration Product Admin) for Atlassian, Account Admin for Databricks, an Organization Owner role for GitHub, Google Admin for Google Workspace, Global Administrator for Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365, Okta Admin plus an Okta API token for an administrative account for Okta, Admin for Salesforce, and Admin or Owner roles for Slack.

quotes: A user with Atlassian Admin privileges.
Jira: User Access Admin
Confluence: Product Admin, User Access Admin
Jira Administration: Product Admin
A user with Account Admin privileges is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to your Databricks organization.
A user with an Organization Owner role in the relevant GitHub organization is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to your GitHub organization.
A user with Google Admin privileges is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to Google Workspace.
A user with Global Administrator privileges is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365.
A user with Okta Admin privileges
An Okta API token for an administrative account in your Okta organization
A user with Admin privileges in the relevant Salesforce organization is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to your Salesforce organization.
A user with Admin or Owner roles is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to Slack workspace.

admin-console-tenant-flow.statement: For Google Workspace, GitHub and Microsoft Azure, clicking Add in the Add Integration window redirects to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console, where the tenant details are entered and the configuration steps for a new SaaS application tenant are completed. The edit steps on those pages say to edit the tenant details and click Save. The Google Workspace and GitHub pages mark a following step as not required for legacy connections, a redirect to the SaaS Application Tenants page where a confirmation window appears, and the Microsoft Azure page marks its following steps as not required for legacy connections.

quotes: You are redirected to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Enter the tenant details and complete the configuration steps required for adding a new SaaS application tenant.
Edit the tenant details as required and click Save.
The following step is not required for legacy connections.
You are redirected to the SaaS Application Tenants page in the Zscaler Admin Console, where a confirmation window appears.
evidence.after: 3. In the Add Integration window, click Add.

quotes: You are redirected to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Enter the tenant details and complete the configuration steps required for adding a new SaaS application tenant.
Edit the tenant details as required and click Save.
The following step is not required for legacy connections.
You are redirected to the SaaS Application Tenants page in the Zscaler Admin Console, where a confirmation window appears.
evidence.after: 3. In the Add Integration window, click Add.

quotes: You are redirected to the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Enter the tenant details and complete the configuration steps required for adding a new SaaS application tenant.
Edit the tenant details as required and click Save.
The following steps are not required for legacy connections.
evidence.after: 3. In the Add Integration window, click Add.

direct-credential-flow.statement: The other platforms connect inside the portal's Add Integration window. Atlassian takes the Atlassian subdomain and an API token, Okta takes the Okta URL and Token, Databricks takes the account ID and the client ID and secret of an account-level service principal assigned the Account Admin role, and Salesforce and Slack show a consent window where all privileges are read-only. Salesforce also offers a Sandbox login.

quotes: In the Add Integration window, enter the Atlassian subdomain and the API token created in the previous section, then click Add.
In the Add Integration window, enter the Okta URL and Token, and then click Connect.
Enter your Databricks Account ID.
Create an account-level service principal.
Assign the Account Admin role to the service principal.
Enter the Client ID and Client secret.
A consent window appears (all privileges are read-only), and you can see a detailed list of permissions and data.
Click Sandbox to log in to your Salesforce Sandbox account.
A consent window appears (all privileges are read-only), and you can see a detailed list of permissions and data.

okta-service-account.statement: For Okta the integration page recommends creating a dedicated service account for integration and assigning it the minimum required privileges.

quotes: Zscaler recommends creating a dedicated service account for integration and assigning the minimum required privileges.

api-token-not-viewable.statement: For Atlassian and Okta, the API token or key cannot be viewed in plain text and must be stored securely. If an Atlassian API token that is in use is revoked, it can be replaced with a new token.

quotes: For security reasons, you cannot view the API token in plain text. You must store the API token securely.
If you revoke an API token that is currently in use, you can replace it with a new token.
For security reasons, you cannot view the API key in plain text. You must store the API key securely.

read-consent-vs-revoke.statement: Additional consent steps are required for revoking and banning applications. On the Atlassian page the first consent step only allows reading of the apps in the workspace, and by default users who are not explicitly granted revocation rights cannot perform revoke operations.

quotes: Additional consent steps are required for the revocation and banning of applications.
This consent step only allows reading of the apps in your workspace.
By default, 3rd-Party App Governance users who are not explicitly granted revocation rights are unable to perform revoke operations.

permissions-google.statement: Google Workspace requests the scopes admin.reports.audit.readonly (Admin, Token and Login activity audit reports), admin.reports.usage.readonly (Login activity reports), admin.directory.group.readonly (groups), admin.directory.user.readonly (users) and admin.directory.user.security (OAuth grants users give to third-party applications).

quotes: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.reports.audit.readonly | Admin, Token, and Login activity audit reports |
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.reports.usage.readonly | Login activity reports |
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.readonly | A list of groups in your Google tenant |
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.readonly | A list of users in your Google tenant |
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.security | OAuth grants your users access to 3rd-party applications |

permissions-github.statement: GitHub requests the scopes read:org (read-only access to organization membership, organization projects and team membership), user:email (read access to a user's email addresses) and read:audit_log (read access to the audit log data).

quotes: | read:org | Read-only access to organization membership, organization projects, and team membership |
| user:email | Grants read access to a user's email addresses |
| read:audit_log | Grants read access to the audit log data |

permissions-azure.statement: Microsoft Azure requests offline_access, AuditLog.Read.All, Directory.Read.All, User.Read.All and Reports.Read.All. Application.ReadWrite.All is an optional permission that is not required for initial onboarding and is only requested for specific activities, such as an admin revoking an app or restricting a particular app's access.

quotes: Maintain access to data you have given access to: offline_access
Read audit log data: AuditLog.Read.All
Read directory data: Directory.Read.All
User.Read.All | User's avatar, basic user information |
Read all usage reports: Reports.Read.All

is an optional permission that can be granted to 3rd-Party App Governance to support additional functionalities. This permission is not required for initial onboarding and is only requested to perform specific activities.
Read and modify applications: Application.ReadWrite.All | Admin revokes an app or restricts a particular app's access |

permissions-atlassian.statement: The Atlassian page's Permissions and Data Collected table lists the permissions used, including offline_access, a global OAuth scope that lets 3rd-Party App Governance refresh the token on expiration without asking for consent repeatedly, and read:me, read:audit-log:jira, read:user:jira, read:permission:jira, read:configuration:confluence and read:group:confluence. The table lists further scopes that are not named here.

quotes: The following table lists the permissions and data collected after integration:
| offline_access | A global OAuth scope, enabling 3rd-Party App Governance to refresh the token upon its expiration to keep the integration live without the need to repetitively ask for consent |
| read:me | View the profile details for the currently logged-in user |
| read:application-role:jira | View application roles |
| read:audit-log:jira | View audit logs |
| read:user:jira | View users |
| read:permission:jira | View permissions |
| read:configuration:confluence | View Confluence settings, themes, and system information |
| read:group:confluence | View details about groups |

permissions-okta.statement: The Okta integration reads /users, /users/…/roles, /groups, /groups/…/users, /groups/…/apps, /apps, /apps/…/users, /apps/…/grants and /api-tokens, where /api-tokens lists API tokens generated in the tenant with their metadata such as token name, the user who generated it, and creation and expiration dates.

quotes: | /users | List of users and their profile attributes, such as name, email, status, and time of last login |
| /users/…/roles | User role assignments (e.g., admin, super admin, user, etc.) |
| /groups | List of user groups which are configured in the tenant
| /groups/…/users | The list of users associated with each of the above groups |
| /groups/…/apps | The list of apps associated with each of the above groups
| /apps | List of apps available in the tenant along with their metadata |
| /apps/…/users | List of users associated with each application |
| /apps/…/grants | For some types of applications, a list of permission scopes granted to the application |
| /api-tokens | List of API tokens that have been generated in the tenant, along with their metadata, such as token name, the user who generated it, and its creation and expiration dates |

permissions-salesforce.statement: Salesforce requests two scopes. The first allows access to the logged-in user's account using APIs such as REST API and Bulk API 2.0 and includes chatter_api, and the second manages user data via web browsers, allows use of access_token on the web, and includes Visualforce.

quotes: | api | Manage user data via APIs.
| web | Manage user data via web browsers.
It allows access to the currently logged-in user’s account using APIs, such as REST API and Bulk API 2.0. This scope also includes chatter_api, which allows access to Connect REST API resources.
Manage user data via web browsers. It allows use of access_token on the web. This scope also includes Visualforce, allowing access to customer-created Visualforce pages.

permissions-slack.statement: Slack requests a permission to view information about your identity, and team:read, users:read, users:read.email, usergroups:read and admin (Administer a workspace). The page says 3rd-Party App Governance uses a very limited set of the APIs granted by the admin permission, designed only to read audit and activity logs.

quotes: 3rd-Party App Governance is utilizing a very limited set of APIs granted by this permission, designed only to read audit and activity logs.
View information about your identity.
View the name, email domain, and icon for workspaces your Slack app is connected to: team:read
View people in a workspace: users:read
View email addresses of people in a workspace: users:read.email
View user groups in a workspace: usergroups:read
Administer a workspace: admin | Collect workspace access logs and applications (integrations) activities such as consent, revoke, and others.

sspm-scan-checkbox.statement: The Okta, Salesforce and Slack pages each say the SSPM Scan checkbox on the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console must be selected to enable the SSPM scan feature for the tenant.

quotes: You must select the SSPM Scan checkbox on the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console to enable the SSPM scan feature for the tenant.
You must select the SSPM Scan checkbox on the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console to enable the SSPM scan feature for the tenant.
You must select the SSPM Scan checkbox on the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console to enable the SSPM scan feature for the tenant.

ingest-delay.statement: After a connection is achieved, pulling and ingesting all relevant application data might take a while depending on the size of the tenant. The Settings page then updates the integration status, first connected time and last synced time, Zscaler emails when the application data and initial insights are viewable in the inventory, and a failed connection shows an error message with the reason.

quotes: After a connection is achieved, it might take a while to pull and ingest all relevant application data depending on the size of your tenant.
the integration status, first connected time, and last synced time are updated on the Settings page.
You then receive an email from Zscaler when the application data and initial insights on applications connected to your platforms are viewable in the inventory.
If the connection fails, an error message appears displaying the reason for the failure.

reconnect.statement: The Atlassian page says it might be necessary to reconnect if an error such as Grant Expired displays. The Google Workspace, GitHub and Microsoft Azure pages say the Reconnect option is available only for legacy tenants, which are the existing tenants onboarded via the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.

quotes: You might need to reconnect Atlassian to 3rd-Party App Governance if an error displays (e.g., Grant Expired).
The Reconnect option is available only for legacy tenants. The existing tenants onboarded via the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal are called legacy tenants.
The Reconnect option is available only for legacy tenants. The existing tenants onboarded via the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal are called legacy tenants.
The Reconnect option is available only for legacy tenants. The existing tenants onboarded via the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal are called legacy tenants.

google-app-blocked.statement: The error This app is blocked can appear when connecting 3rd-Party App Governance to Google Workspace, because company settings might prevent connecting third-party apps without explicitly trusting them. The page resolves it by adding 3rd-Party App Governance to the trusted apps in the Google Admin Console under Security > API Controls, entering client ID 1017448667100-p63ee1484o66sdnfreusoafl8hp9oci5.apps.googleusercontent.com with Trusted: can access all Google services selected.

quotes: The error message This app is blocked appears when connecting 3rd-Party App Governance to your Google Workspace.
Occasionally, company settings might prevent connecting to third-party apps without explicitly trusting them.
To resolve this issue, add 3rd-Party App Governance to your Google Workspace trusted apps.
In the Google Admin Console, go to Security > API Controls.
Enter the following client ID: 1017448667100-p63ee1484o66sdnfreusoafl8hp9oci5.apps.googleusercontent.com.
Make sure Trusted: can access all Google services is selected, and then click Configure.

google-ou-segregation.statement: Segregating a Google Workspace integration by organizational units (OUs) is a feature in limited availability.

quotes: You can segregate your Google Workspace integration by organizational units (OUs). This feature is in limited availability.

settings-tenants.statement: The Settings page shows the SaaS tenants added in 3rd-Party App Governance and Advanced SSPM. The tenants can be filtered by Status, Platform or Enabled Features and exported to a CSV file, and Enabled Features can be App Governance, SSPM Scan, or both.

quotes: The Settings page allows you to view and manage Software as a Service (SaaS) tenants added in 3rd-Party App Governance and Advanced SSPM.
Filter the tenants by Status, Platform, or Enabled Features.
Export the tenants report to a CSV file.
Enabled Features: The feature that is enabled for the tenant. It can be App Governance, SSPM Scan, or both.

settings-tenant-status.statement: A tenant's integration status is Healthy (the integration completed successfully), Unhealthy (failure to achieve a connection; contact Zscaler Support) or Onboarding (connection achieved and data being ingested). If the tenant has yet to sync, N/A displays for the last sync, and if the duration of the sync is excessive, the last sync time is highlighted in red.

quotes: Healthy: The integration is completed successfully.
Unhealthy: Failure to achieve a connection. Contact Zscaler Support if you require further assistance.
Onboarding: Connection is achieved and 3rd-Party App Governance is ingesting the relevant data.
If the tenant has yet to sync, N/A displays. If the duration of the sync is excessive, the last sync time is highlighted in red.

okta-service-account-role.summary: The Okta page's heading and recommendation describe a dedicated read-only service account with minimum privileges, and its steps then assign that account the Super Administrator role.

quotes: To create a dedicated read-only service account:
Zscaler recommends creating a dedicated service account for integration and assigning the minimum required privileges.

positions.says: The service account is described as read-only, with the minimum required privileges.

quotes: Select the 3rd-Party App Governance service account, set the role to Super Administrator, and click Save.

positions.says: The step sets the service account's role to Super Administrator.

okta-service-account-role.impact: The page does not say whether Super Administrator is the minimum role the integration needs or a documentation error, so the privilege to grant the Okta service account is not settled by this page.

databricks-permissions.title: What permissions the Databricks integration requests
databricks-permissions.detail: The Databricks page describes the account ID and service principal inputs but gives no permissions table, unlike the Google Workspace, GitHub, Microsoft Azure, Atlassian, Okta, Salesforce and Slack pages.

sync-cadence.title: How often a platform is resynced and what an excessive sync is
sync-cadence.detail: The Settings page highlights an excessive sync duration in red, and the pages do not say how often the portal resyncs a platform or what duration counts as excessive.

chrome-and-extra-platforms.title: How platforms in the risk score table that cannot be connected get into the inventory
chrome-and-extra-platforms.detail: The App Panel risk-score table names ServiceNow, Box, Zoom, Webex and Chrome Extensions, which are not in the list of platforms that connect to 3rd-Party App Governance. The pages give the Chrome extensions CSV export and upload as one route and no route for the others.
